_comment: A map recipe (#331, decision 0010): the land before anything is placed on it. size: the square map's side in metres, centred on the origin. relief: metres from the lowest to the highest the noise reaches. hill_mask: a slow noise (frequency, 1 / metres) whose value between from and to fades hilly country in; outside it lies near-flat lowland. layers: noise summed for the height, each with frequency, amplitude (share of relief), octaves, and masked (only where the hill mask says hilly, and only rising out of the lowland). walkable: max_grade (rise per metre a player still walks easily), min_share (the least share of the map that gentle), flat_grade and min_flat_share (near-flat ground for towns and fields, and how much of it the map needs), hillside_grade and min_hillside_share (real hillsides: the least share of the map that rises at least this much); the tests hold every seed to these. water: ponds where water would collect: the land is surveyed every cell metres, a basin at least min_depth deep and min_area square metres becomes a pond (shrunk to max_area by lowering its level), its level freeboard metres below where it would spill, its bed deepen times deeper than the land. biomes: noise fields for forest, dry grass and rock (frequency 1 / metres, threshold where a field starts), then shaped by the land: rock shows on ground steeper than rock_grade_from, fully past rock_grade_to, in patches rock_patch_frequency (1 / metres) apart; woods grow on the hills (hill_forest of the way) and in a few broad woodland regions (woodland_frequency, at most lowland_forest), the forest field cutting clearings into them; none in water. map_metres_per_texel: the terrain shader's biome map resolution. zones: the land classified every cell metres into water, wetland (within wet_distance of water), slope (steeper than slope_grade), hilltop (hilltop_rise metres above the ground hilltop_ring metres round it), forest (woods above forest_cutoff), flat (under flat_grade) and open (the rest); touching cells of a kind make a zone. uses: per use, the kinds it may go on and the smallest area (square metres) it needs. spawn_margin and spawn_edge: the player camp's spot, between this many metres from the map's edge. settlements: the city's footprint is the largest square of its zone's cells, at least city.size metres; up to town.max towns, at least town.size, town.spacing metres from the city and each other; the camp stays camp.clearance metres outside them; every settlement stays edge_margin metres in from the map's edge.
